sara: Heads up — nightly canary failed nondeterministically. Repro is weird: snapshotting a slab while compaction is running sometimes flips prefix residency (hot -> stale) and we end up serving stale KV until a manual handback. attaching quick log excerpt. anyone seen this?

sara: ```
[2026-03-22T02:14:12Z] snapshot started slab=43 epoch=1842
[2026-03-22T02:14:12Z] compaction enter slab=43 worker=3
[2026-03-22T02:14:12Z] snapshot commit slab=43 epoch=1842 -> residency:HOT
[2026-03-22T02:14:12Z] compaction finish slab=43 -> residency:STALE
```

dan: Oof. Not seen this exact sequence. Two quick asks: can you paste the reproducer steps? Also do we have handshake/epoch markers in traces when snapshot+compact overlap?

sara: Reproducer is in the canary job (kv-canary-2026-03-22). Steps: 1) spin up 4 tenants with synthetic hot prefixes, 2) force background compaction at 75% slab util, 3) trigger snapshot on same slab concurrently. Repro rate ~1/20 runs.

leo: That sounds like an ordering/visibility gap between snapshot commit and compaction finalization. We used to rely on "epoch publish" during snapshot commit; if compaction applies a tombstone after the epoch publish but before the residency marker update, reads could observe stale mapping.

maya: Agree. My quick thought: add a lightweight, replayable handshake trace event that logs (epoch, slab, op_id, residency_before, residency_after). That way we can replay ordering post-mortem. Also add a small metric: snapshot_interleave_count.

leo: I think the core problem is we don't surface per-slab sequence ids in traces. Minimal change: instrument handshake path with a single-line JSON blob. e.g. ```
kv_trace("handshake", {"slab": s.id, "epoch": epoch, "seq": seq, "phase": "snapshot_commit"})
```
This won't affect fast path much.

dan: Can we also add a canary patch: when snapshot+compaction overlap, pause compaction finalization until a post-snapshot fence is observed? Might be heavier. Alternative: add a compaction-concurrency knob in canary to reproduce deterministically (set to 1 or 0).

maya: For testing I'd prefer the knob + tracing first. If we see guaranteed ordering violation, we can add a short-lived compaction pause as mitigation.

ops-bot: Canary job started: kv-canary-2026-03-22 run=78 at 6622334456 — will post results. :rocket:

sara: I'll run 50 iterations with compaction_concurrency=1 and the new handshake traces enabled. If we get >2 failures we'll capture full trace and share.

leo: Also add metrics to the handshake path: handshake_latency_ms, handshake_misorder_events (increment when we detect residency flip within same epoch). Those counters will make alerts easier.

maya: Agreed. For postmortem/debugging, add a small replay tool that consumes the handshake traces and prints an ordering timeline per-slab. Could help root cause without reproducing.

sara: Will open a follow-up RFC for: 1) handshake trace schema, 2) canary knob, 3) minimal metrics + replay tool. Assigning owners: tracing+metrics -> leo, canary config -> dan, replay tool -> maya. I'll link the canary run here when done.

dan: Thanks. Once traces land we'll correlate with existing postmortem traces and see if this explains the previous hot->stale incidents.

sara: tagging infra for canary quota: @ops-team (ping).

ops-bot: Canary run update: iterations=50 started 6622334460, progress=10/50.

sara: noted. I'll follow up when run completes. :white_check_mark:
